beats.title: Count the starter in the ratio
beats.outcome: Make a reasoned choice and name the evidence that would change it.
beats.explanation: [[hearth-m02-concept|Hydration]] is water divided by flour. The starter carries both, so the true figure counts it. A recipe that looks like 73% from its lines can be 76% in the bowl, and the dough will feel it.

handbook.markdown: A starter at 100% hydration adds equal weights of flour and water. Add them to the listed lines before dividing. If the starter is not ready yet, [revisit reading a starter](#/module/hearth-m01/hearth-m01-starter) first.

beats.recap: Hydration is water divided by flour.

beats.title: Match folds to hydration
beats.outcome: Make a reasoned choice and name the evidence that would change it.
beats.explanation: A wetter dough spreads unless you build strength. Plan more sets of folds and a firmer pre-shape as hydration rises, and raise the water in small steps once shaping is reliable.

handbook.markdown: Folds build structure gradually. Space them through the first half of the bulk ferment and stop once the dough holds a rounded shape for a few minutes.

beats.recap: A wetter dough spreads unless you build strength.

recap.title: Hydration and dough strength: what to keep
recap.markdown: Read the evidence the loaf gives you, change one thing at a time and write down what you saw.
